To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the EGFR-dependent C15 and Notch-regulated BOWL homeodomain and zinc-finger transcriptional repressing factors, respectively, interact with the LAE bric-àbrac enhancer to refine gene expression in the Drosophila appendage.

the EGFR-activated transcription factors, the C15 and Bowl proteins, act together on the LAE enhancers of the bab2 gene to repress its expression in the proximal leg, in a timely manner and in response to the Notch signaling pathway.
the Drosophila bric-àbrac2 (bab 2) gene is the direct target of two transcriptional regulators, the C15 homeoprotein and the Bowl repressor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic and molecular mechanisms that govern limb morphogenesis in Drosophila.
the mechanisms by which transcription factors integrate cell signaling inputs to refine gene expression in a tissue-specific manner.

the mechanisms of tissue-specific enhancer regulation by transcriptional activators and repressors, which integrate cell signaling inputs to refine gene expression in a timely manner during development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
C15 and Bwl act as transcriptional repressing duo to control the expression of rn and bab2 during leg morphogenesis.
the LAE enhancers are subject to multiple and complex regulatory inputs that include transcriptional activators and repressors acting on a common enhancer element.
the Dll/Rn transcription factors activate the bab2 gene in the distal region of the leg, while the C15/Bowl repressors inhibit bab2 transcription in the proximal region of the leg.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Drosophila bab2 gene is a direct target of the EGFR and Notch signaling pathways, and is controlled by a complex regulatory mechanism involving the interplay of multiple transcription factors.

the LAE is a complex and dynamic regulatory element, which integrates multiple inputs, including cell signaling pathways and transcription factors, to control bab2 expression in a tissue-specific manner.
the transcription factor network that controls leg morphogenesis is finely tuned by a molecular integration of cell signals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
transcriptional regulation is a dynamic and highly flexible process, which is achieved through the integration of various signaling inputs, and the deployment of multiple transcriptional regulators.

the LAE enhancers of bric-àbrac2, which are activated by Dll/Rn and repressed by C15/Bowl, are a good example of how cell signaling pathways can regulate the activity of enhancers through the recruitment of transcriptional regulators.
the Dll activators are not only required for the establishment of the leg primordium but also for the maintenance of the leg identity.
